title: Testing Suite
content:
**Testing Suite** is Photon's validation backbone. Built on the **Bun Test kernel**, it executes your entire integration matrix in milliseconds by eliminating the TCP network stack from the feedback loop.

The Validation Engine

Testing in Photon isn't about simulating HTTP; it's about executing the request-response lifecycle directly in memory. This approach provides 100% fidelity with production behavior while maintaining unit-test performance.

ZERO_IO_TESTS

Bypasses the physical network layer. Requests are dispatched directly to the router kernel via memory buffers.

FLUENT_ASSERT

Readable, chainable assertions for status codes, JSON structures, and database state. Built for expressiveness.

ISOLATED_BOOT

Fast-boot core instances for every test. No state leakage between parallel test execution workers.

Testing Standalone Photon Apps

Test Photon handlers directly without starting a TCP server. Ideal for microservices and small logic units.

import { test, expect } from 'bun:test'
import { Photon } from '@gravito/photon'

const app = new Photon()
app.get('/ping', (c) => c.text('pong'))

test('ping route returns pong', async () => {
  const res = await app.fetch(new Request('http://localhost/ping'))
  expect(res.status).toBe(200)
  expect(await res.text()).toBe('pong')
})

Integration with PlanetCore

Using createHttpTester provides the ultimate fluent interface for full-stack integration testing.

import { describe, it, beforeEach } from 'bun:test'
import { PlanetCore, createHttpTester } from '@gravito/core'

describe('User API', () => {
  let tester: any

  beforeEach(async () => {
    const core = await PlanetCore.boot({ /* config */ })
    tester = createHttpTester(core)
  })

  it('can list users', async () => {
    const response = await tester.get('/api/users')
    await response.assertOk().assertJson({ users: [] })
  })
})

Supported HTTP Methods

The tester mimics human interaction through a high-level API:

await tester.get('/api/users')
await tester.post('/api/users', { name: 'Carl' }) // Auto JSON serialization
await tester.put('/api/users/1', { name: 'Updated' })
await tester.delete('/api/users/1')
await tester.get('/api/users', { 'Authorization': 'Bearer token' })

Fluent Assertions Matrix

The TestResponse object exposes an extensive list of semantic assertions to keep your test code dry and readable.

Status Checks

  • .assertOk() (200)
  • .assertCreated() (201)
  • .assertNotFound() (404)
  • .assertForbidden() (403)

Content Verification

  • .assertSee('text')
  • .assertJson({ id: 1 })
  • .assertJsonStructure({ data: [] })
  • .assertHeader('key', 'val')

Database & State Testing

Reset the universe between tests using Atlas migrations and factories for predictable data seeding.

beforeEach(async () => {
  await DB.migrate('fresh')
})

it('seeds via factories', async () => {
  const user = await UserFactory.new().create()
  expect(user.id).toBeDefined()
})

Mocking & Service Swapping

Leverage the IoC container to swap real services with mocks, ensuring your tests remain side-effect free.

it('mocks mail delivery', async () => {
  const mockMail = { send: mock(() => Promise.resolve()) }
  core.container.instance('mail', mockMail)

  const res = await tester.post('/register', { email: 't@dev.io' })
  await res.assertOk()
  expect(mockMail.send).toHaveBeenCalled()
})

// SPEC: IN_MEMORY_DISPATCH_PROTOCOL

Photon's testing layer doesn't open a port. It mocks the `Request` and `Response` fetch objects directly at the adapter boundary, meaning your tests run 50x faster than traditional `supertest` or `axios` based setups.

Performance: Feedback Cycle

Comparison of test suite execution time for 1,000 integration tests.

PHOTON_TEST_SUITE ~0.8s Total
TRADITIONAL_JEST_AXIOS ~42.0s Total

**Architect's Insight:** Slow tests are the death of productivity. We built the testing suite to be as invisible as the engine itself. By keeping everything in-memory and leveraging Bun's native parallelism, we turn testing into a real-time validation stream.
